entries.title: Quote to customer PO, sales order and work order
entries.text: Start in Sales > Quotes. Add a customer and quote lines, send or revise the quote, then record the customer's purchase order reference when converting to a sales order. A customer PO is not your supplier purchase order. Sales orders track demand, fulfillment and shipping. Create linked work orders for manufacturing, then kit, build, inspect and ship. Manufacturing production work orders require a matching CERTIFIED BOM. Review each resulting record; do not assume a quote automatically completes manufacturing or posts cash.

entries.title: Work order types, standalone production and optional prototype BOM certification
entries.text: The prototype step is optional. A DRAFT or IN_REVIEW BOM can be certified directly for production when Prototype required is off. When Prototype required is on, prototype evidence is required before production certification. Only CERTIFIED BOM revisions for the same part can be used to create, release or start PRODUCTION work orders. A standalone production WO still requires a certified BOM; it does not require a sales order. TASK_ONLY, REWORK, INSPECTION, REPAIR and PROTOTYPE are separate types with their own rules, not ways to bypass production certification. Certification uses the signer's PIN, locks the revision and obsoletes the previous certified revision. To change a certified or obsolete BOM, create a new revision. Never tell users prototype is mandatory for all BOMs.

entries.title: PIN electronic signatures and traveler steps
entries.text: Set or change your electronic sign-off PIN under My Account. A password is not the sign-off PIN. Enter the PIN only in the application's signature field, never in AI chat or a support message. Traveler and inspection sign-offs require the appropriate permission and PIN verification; they record the signer. Controlled Docs signatures bind to an exact revision and content hash. The assistant cannot sign, approve or bypass a signature. If a signature fails, check your PIN setup, permissions, step prerequisites and current revision, then contact human support if it persists.

entries.title: Kitting shortages and completing work orders versus traveler steps
entries.text: Work Orders tracks planned, released, kitted and in-progress manufacturing work. Kitting shows upcoming kits and material shortages. Planning/MRP and purchase requests help cover missing material. Receipt and putaway can update kit readiness. Production start checks the certified BOM and kit prerequisites; inspect blockers instead of forcing status changes. Travelers carry the work instructions and sign-off steps. Completing a WO is different from completing one traveler step and does not mean a customer shipment or invoice has been completed.

entries.title: Purchase orders, receiving travelers and serialized stock
entries.text: Purchasing handles purchase requests, approval and supplier POs. Receiving uses receiving travelers for supplier deliveries and customer-furnished property. Work through the receipt, inspection and putaway steps; partial receipts remain distinct from closing the PO. Serialized items need the required individual serial records and quantities, not just a free-text serial note. Trace/Serials shows as-built genealogy. Quarantined or rejected material must follow quality disposition, not be silently returned to available stock. Review quantities and serials if receiving or PO closure is blocked.

entries.title: QA, NCR, MRB and corrective action
entries.text: QA Inspection records inspections. NCR/Quality tracks nonconformances; MRB handles material review and disposition; CAR tracks corrective action and root cause. RMA is for customer returns. Quality Programs includes calibration, audits, tool control, ESD, FOD, HAZMAT, safety and counterfeit controls. Use the relevant review and authorization workflow before disposition or closing a case. An NCR is not a CAR and creating a CAR does not by itself release held material. The software supports compliance records; it does not guarantee AS9100, CMMC or DCAA certification.

entries.title: Engineering PLM, work instructions and traveler steps
entries.text: Products is the PLM product catalog. Engineering tracks engineering work; Requirements tracks requirements and verification coverage. BOMs, Work Instructions and Test Procedures define controlled product and build information. Config Management handles engineering changes and baselines. Use revisions and controlled change review rather than editing a released definition in place. Work instructions supply traveler steps; test procedures support acceptance and functional testing. Existence of a screen is not proof that an integration or automatic downstream action is configured.

entries.title: PMO programs, projects, WBS, budgets and earned value
entries.text: PMO organizes programs, projects, work breakdown structures, PI planning and alerts. Budgets define direct or indirect charge codes and enacted budget authority. Projects can link manufacturing and costs. Earned value uses planned value, earned value and actual cost: SPI is earned value divided by planned value; CPI is earned value divided by actual cost. Values depend on the underlying records and do not certify financial accuracy. Review program policy and budget approval before spending; the assistant cannot enact a budget.

entries.title: Accounting, AR/AP posting and GovCon
entries.text: Accounting includes the general ledger, journals, AR/AP, financial reports, payroll and bank reconciliation. GovCon Contracts & Rates tracks contracts, CLINs, indirect rates, job costs and unallowable cost treatment. Post source documents through their workflow and verify the resulting ledger entries; do not create a manual duplicate journal to hide a failed posting. If AR/AP posting, reversal or reconciliation fails, capture the record reference and use human support. Do not claim payments, payroll tax filing, bank feeds or regulatory certification are automatic merely because a screen exists. Consult a qualified accountant for accounting or legal advice.

entries.title: Tenant Docs knowledge base
entries.text: Docs is the tenant's internal knowledge base: spaces, hierarchical pages, templates, version history, backlinks and record links. Editors save new revisions; concurrent edits are version-checked. Use page history to inspect an earlier version and restore it as a new saved revision, preserving history. Controlled page signatures bind to a revision and its content hash using PIN verification. This assistant's product help uses reviewed in-repository guidance, not private company Docs or arbitrary uploaded instructions. It cannot read or disclose another company's pages.

entries.title: Permissions, identity and safe support
entries.text: Access depends on the signed-in user, assigned role, permissions and tenant. A menu item or a guided tour does not grant permission. Ask a company administrator to review a missing module or denied action; do not switch identities, forge cookies or bypass a permission check. The AI help assistant is read-only: it explains procedures but does not create, finish, delete, post, approve, sign or modify ERP records. It does not fetch live plant, HR, payroll or other tenant data. For live status, open the authorized module. Use Help & Support for a human; submitting a ticket is a separate user action.

entries.title: First setup, configure your shop and quick navigation menus
entries.text: Start with company setup and users, then catalog items, customers, suppliers and controlled manufacturing definitions. Set a sign-off PIN in My Account. Use Guides for interactive walkthroughs and Ctrl-K or Command-K for navigation. Begin with a small end-to-end test: quote, sales order, certified BOM, work order, kit, traveler sign-offs, receiving/stock, shipment and accounting review. Import and integration availability must be checked in the actual module; do not assume every external ERP or bank is connected. Human help is available through the Help & Support tab.

entries.title: Carina AI help, privacy, limits and human escalation
entries.text: Carina is Protessera's existing AI assistant powered by Grok from xAI, not a separate text model. It can make mistakes. Chat, optional voice, language preferences and guided tours are available from the existing Help bubble; settings are at My AI Assistant. It is read-only product help grounded in reviewed product guides, with source links and page context. It does not access live records or execute changes. General questions and answers and thumbs feedback are logged in the current tenant's audit log for review, with common secrets redacted. Do not enter secrets, PINs, passwords, personal, export-controlled or other sensitive data; question text is sent to xAI when an AI response is requested. If uncertain, unavailable or contradicted by the current screen, use the Support tab for a human. Rate limits and request budgets protect availability and cost; no automatic ticket is sent.

entries.title: Getting started with Protessera
entries.text:
A guided lap around the whole system — every area and how it connects.
Welcome to Protessera 👋: This tour walks the whole system, area by area. Use Next/Back to move, or the X to leave anytime. Turn on the speaker to have each step read aloud. Protessera runs your entire shop — sales, engineering, purchasing, production, quality, and accounting — as one connected flow, so data entered once follows the work everywhere.
The sidebar is your map: Every module lives here, grouped by area. Click a group heading to collapse it; the rail remembers what you close.
Search anything, fast: Press ⌘K / Ctrl-K from anywhere to jump to a work order, PO, part, customer, or module by name or keyword. You rarely need to hunt through menus — search is the fastest way to anything.
Your action items: The bell shows what's waiting on you — approvals, MRB holds, buyer packages, overdue reviews. The badge is the count.
Manufacturing: Work Orders, Workcenters, the Test Center, Kitting, and Planning/MRP — where jobs are built and tracked on the floor.
Engineering & PLM: Requirements, BOMs, Work Instructions, Test Procedures, Products, and Configuration Management — the controlled product definition.
Supply Chain: Items, Purchasing, Receiving, Suppliers/ASL, Inventory, Government Property, and Assets — everything about buying and holding material.
Quality & Compliance: QA inspection, NCR/MRB/CAR, RMA, serial trace, and the Quality Programs suite (calibration, tool control, ESD, FOD, HAZMAT, safety, audits, counterfeit).
Programs & Business: Reports, PMO & PI planning, Budgets, Accounting, Payroll, and HR — the money and program side of the house.
Guides live here: This ? button opens the Guides hub any time. The tours below walk real end-to-end flows — try 'Order to cash' or 'Work order lifecycle' next.

entries.title: Your daily workspace: approvals & timecard
entries.text:
Where your own to-dos, approvals, and time entry live.
My Approvals: Everything waiting on your decision collects here — PTO, timesheets, expenses, and purchasing approvals — so nothing sits in an inbox. Approvals route to the person who owns the decision, not to a generic queue, so accountability is always clear.
My Timesheet: Log hours by day against charge codes / work orders and submit for the pay period. Your manager approves from their own queue. Time charged here feeds job cost, budgets, and payroll — one entry, many downstream uses.
My Account: Change your password, manage sessions, and set your sign-off PIN used to electronically sign inspections and approvals.

entries.title: Order to cash: quote → sales order → ship
entries.text:
Follow a customer order from quotation through shipment.
It starts with a customer: Customers hold accounts, credit limits, and payment terms. Quotes and sales orders both pull from here, and credit is checked before an order books.
Draft a quote: Start a new quote here — add line items and pricing, then email it to the customer straight from the module. The lifecycle is Draft → sent → customer PO recorded. Quotes capture what you promised at what price — the basis for the order and later margin analysis.
Record their PO → sales order: When the customer accepts, record their PO number and convert the quote into a sales order in one step. No re-keying — pricing and lines flow straight from the accepted quote onto the order.
The sales order drives production: Sales Orders track each order through Open/Planned → In Production → Ready to Ship → Shipped. From here work orders are created to build what was sold.
Pack & ship: Ready orders land in the shipping queue. Pack them, generate the packing list, and record the shipment against the sales order. Shipping closes the loop back to the order and to accounting for invoicing.

entries.title: Work order lifecycle: release → kit → build → test → done
entries.text:
How a job moves from release through the floor to completion.
Work Orders run the build: Create a production WO straight from a BOM (or a task-only WO for non-BOM work). The WO carries what to build, how many, the routing of steps, and its traveler. The WO is the spine of the shop — kitting, labor, test, and quality all attach to it.
Kitting pulls the material: When a WO is ready, kitting picks its BOM components. A complete kit pulls everything; a short kit does a partial pick and flags the shortage. Picked material stages to a real location tagged to the WO, so you can see exactly where a kit is sitting.
The Production Floor is live: The floor view shows every active job and where it is right now. Operators move a WO between work centers as they work it.
Work centers do the work: Each work center (cell, machine, or station) has capacity and a queue. Labor is clocked against the WO at the center where the step runs. Clocked labor feeds job cost and the capacity picture Planning uses.
Powered functional test: Work in the TEST area runs through the Test Center — run acceptance/functional procedures against a unit and record pass/fail results. Test results attach to the serial's as-built record for traceability.
Completion closes it out: A finished WO reports completion at Receiving putaway, relieves its kit, and moves finished goods into inventory ready to ship.

entries.title: Planning & MRP: forecast → material sheets → dated WOs
entries.text:
Rough-cut capacity and the forecast-to-work-order flow.
Planning balances demand & capacity: Rough-cut capacity across the horizon at a glance — plant utilization, scheduled load vs. available hours, and unscheduled backlog — against a working calendar, flagging late or undated work.
Forecast → MRS → MWO: A forecast drives material requirement sheets (MRS), which release dated manufacturing work orders (MWOs). Buy demand flows on to Purchasing. This is how demand becomes both the jobs to build and the parts to buy, with real need-by dates.

entries.title: Live shop visibility: floor, radiators, value stream
entries.text:
The big-screen and flow views that show shop state at a glance.
Info Radiators: Wall-display dashboards for the floor — live throughput, WIP, and exceptions sized for a big screen. The tiles rotate through slides on their own.
Value Stream Map: Each stage of the flow shows its health — healthy, watch, or constrained — so you can see where work piles up between steps. Managing the constraint is how you actually move the whole line faster.

entries.title: Product definition: requirements → BOM → WI → test
entries.text:
How the controlled product definition is built and released.
Requirements come first: Capture 'shall' statements, trace each to the work that implements it, and record the verification method. Coverage shows what's still uncovered. Traceability from requirement to verification is the backbone of an auditable design.
BOMs define structure: Bills of material hold the product structure and revisions. Part numbers themselves live in Items — the BOM references them and shows where-used.
Work Instructions tell the floor how: Step-by-step build instructions with photos, tools, and sign-offs. Released WIs are retained as controlled masters in CM.
Test Procedures define acceptance: Acceptance and functional test procedures (ATPs) are CM-controlled and run at the Test Center, recording results per step.
Products tie it together (PLM): The product record links its BOM, WIs, procedures, and program — the single lifecycle view of what you make.

entries.title: Configuration Management & the change process
entries.text:
Controlled documents, numbering, and the ECR/ECO workflow.
Submissions, Library & Numbers: CM has three tabs: Submissions (change requests in flight), Library (released controlled documents with revision chains), and Numbers (schemes + the master registry). Nothing on the floor should reference an uncontrolled copy; CM guarantees one released master per number.
Changes go through an ECR: A change is proposed as a submission (ECR), routed to approvers, and released — which revs the document and archives the prior master. Numbering ensures every document draws from a controlled sequence. This is the same controlled path Quality Program policies now follow — submit a policy and it lands here as an ECR until released.
Engineering executes the work: The Engineering board tracks design tasks by discipline (systems, mechanical, electrical, software, and more), tying effort back to requirements and changes.

entries.title: Procure to receive: PR → approval → PO → receiving
entries.text:
A buy from request through approval, buyer packaging, PO, and receipt.
Every buy starts as a PR: A purchase request captures what's needed, the quantity, and the charge (project/WBS, work order, or overhead). Manufacturing and project buys must use catalog parts. Charging the buy correctly here is what keeps job cost and budgets honest downstream.
Approvals route to the charge owner: The PR routes to whoever owns the charge — a WBS owner, program, or budget holder — never to purchasing itself. Toggle between Purchase orders and Purchase requests here; each PR shows its approval status. Spend is controlled by the person accountable for the money, not the person doing the buying.
A buyer packages it: An assigned buyer confirms prices, attaches the supplier quote, notes any sole-source justification, then converts the approved PR into a purchase order.
Receiving with travelers: Incoming material is received against the PO on a dock traveler, inspected, and put away. Government-furnished property is flagged separately.
Stock lands in Inventory: After put-away, material shows by location — on-hand, available, committed, and quarantine. Material only becomes 'available' after put-away, so kitting never grabs stock still on the dock.

entries.title: Items & inventory: the part master and stock
entries.text:
Part numbers, sourcing, and how on-hand stock is tracked.
Items are the part master: Part numbers, sourcing, standard costs, and approved vendors live in this table — separate from BOMs, which reference these items.
Inventory by location: On-hand by bin with lot/serial tracking, government-furnished vs. company stock, and quarantine for held material. Lot and serial tracking is what makes full genealogy and recalls possible.
Kanban replenishment: Parts at or below their minimum with nothing on order surface as shortages — a Kanban signal that raises a replenishment PR before you run out.

entries.title: Suppliers, ASL & government property
entries.text:
Approved suppliers, scorecards, and DFARS-tracked GFP.
Approved Supplier List: Each row is an approved supplier. Open one for its ASL line items, POs, invoices, QMS certifications, and a performance scorecard. Buying from an approved, scored supplier is a flow-down requirement in AS9100 shops.
Government property (GFP): Government-furnished property is tracked apart from company stock with UID, DD-1149 movement, and DFARS accountability.
Asset tracker: Tools, test equipment, and demo units with check-out/check-in — total, available, and checked-out at a glance. Intangibles like software licenses live under Virtual Assets.

entries.title: Quality escape: inspection → NCR → MRB → CAR
entries.text:
How a defect is caught, dispositioned, and prevented from recurring.
QA catches it first: Visual, GD&T, and continuity inspections run in the QA queue (powered functional test is the Test Center). A failure here becomes a nonconformance.
Nonconformances & yield: The Quality module logs NCRs and tracks yield and inspection trends. A significant NCR escalates to the Material Review Board.
The MRB dispositions material: The board decides: use-as-is, rework, repair, scrap, or return to supplier — with justification. Scrap can auto-raise a replacement PR; rework/repair open a linked work order.
Link the case to the quality programs: On each case you can pin a suspect calibration tool (and decide to pull it for recal), or flag the failure as ESD/FOD/counterfeit-caused — which auto-opens an incident in that program that runs its disposition steps. This closes the loop from a defect back to its systemic cause instead of just dispositioning the parts.
A CAR prevents recurrence: Switch to the CAR view (Corrective Action) from the toggle at the top. A disposition can open a CAR — root cause, corrective action, and verification — so the problem doesn't come back.

entries.title: Returns & traceability: RMA and serial genealogy
entries.text:
Handle a customer return and trace a serial's full as-built history.
RMA handles returns: Each row is a return authorization — receive the unit and route it to MRB or a repair work order. The RMA links back to the original order and serial.
Serial traceability: Pick a serial to walk its genealogy — the as-built tree, the lots and sub-serials that went into it, and every test and disposition it touched. Full genealogy answers 'what else is affected?' in a recall or escape investigation in seconds.

entries.title: Quality Programs: calibration & tool control
entries.text:
Gage calibration, toolboxes, labels/DXF, and missing/broken tool reports.
The Quality Programs hub: One place for the whole QMS suite — calibration, tool control, HAZMAT, ESD, FOD, safety, internal audits, and counterfeit — each a card showing overdue and due-soon counts.
Every program has a controlled policy: This card links the program's policy — a CM-controlled document. Submit a new one and it enters the CM change process as an ECR; or link an existing CM document. It publishes only when CM releases it. Policies follow the same controlled path as work instructions, so nothing on the floor references an uncontrolled copy.
Add a gage — attach the certificate: Enter the ID, interval, and next-due, then attach the calibration certificate as a file (not a link). Interval and next-due line up so it's quick to fill.
The register + label / DXF: Each gage shows its status and next-due. Log a passing calibration and the due date rolls forward automatically. Use the label link to print a tag or download a DXF to laser-etch the ID.
Toolboxes & tools: Add a toolbox (named by its workcenter location) and add tools to it. Toggle 'needs calibration' on a tool and it also appears on the Calibration register with its own cadence.
Tool checks & missing/broken reports: Run a toolbox inspection that ticks each tool and saves the report to history. From any tool, open a report: BROKEN gathers pieces and one-clicks a replacement PR; MISSING (or an unrecoverable piece) auto-opens a FOD incident. A lost tool is a foreign-object risk — the workflow forces it through the FOD process instead of being forgotten.

entries.title: Quality Programs: inspections, incidents & audits
entries.text:
ESD/FOD walks, humidity, MRB-linked incidents, internal audits, and counterfeit.
ESD stations — inspect from the register: Each station carries an 'Inspect' pill. Define the inspection template once (below the register) and it applies to every station; running one records pass/fail, notes, and photos to a clickable history.
Humidity tracking: A humidity device can POST relative humidity per area to /api/esd/humidity (or you log it by hand). Readings show against the 30–70% ESD-safe band, flagging out-of-band areas.
FOD walks: Add FOD zones (no location needed — the zone is the place) and run walks with the same template workflow: customize what to look for, attach photos, and save each walk.
Internal audits: Add an audit by picking the program you're auditing, then run it step-by-step. Mark each clause OK, OFI, or NCR with evidence photos — every NCR opens a tracked corrective action with a reinspect-by date.
Counterfeit prevention: Log a suspect part with photo evidence and optionally initiate an MRB case from it. Suspect-counterfeit findings in MRB flow back here to be tracked and dispositioned.
HAZMAT — area & expiration: HAZMAT materials are assigned to a workcenter/area, carry the SDS attached to the record, and track a material expiration date separately — expired and expiring items are flagged right in the register.

entries.title: Program management: PMO, PI planning & budgets
entries.text:
Run programs with WBS, earned value, increments, and charge codes.
The PMO runs programs: Programs and portfolios group the projects beneath them, each with a work-breakdown structure and earned-value metrics (SPI/CPI) — schedule and cost performance at a glance.
PI planning: Program-increment planning lays out the next block of work across teams — the SAFe-style cadence for committing scope.
PM alerts: Unread program risks and threshold breaches surface here (and on the bell) so a slipping program gets attention early.
Budgets & charge codes: The charge-code owner approves time and material against the budget. Forecast work is direct job cost; standalone budgets are company indirect. This is where PRs and timesheets actually hit a budget, tying execution to the money.

entries.title: Accounting: GL, AR/AP, payroll & banking
entries.text:
The books — period close, receivables/payables, pay runs, and bank feeds.
The general ledger & close: Accounting runs on your basis (accrual/cash) and fiscal calendar — journals, P&L, balance sheet, AR, and AP. Month-end close locks the period so posted books can't shift.
Banking & payroll are tabs here: Switch areas from this bar. Banking links accounts via Plaid to pull transactions and reconcile against the ledger; Payroll runs gross-to-net from approved timesheets. Because time is charged to jobs and budgets, labor cost flows to both payroll and job cost from one source.
Reports & export: Run any report on screen, download CSV for Excel, or print — aging, valuation, WIP, and more, on live data with no setup.

entries.title: HR & hiring: workforce → recruit → onboard
entries.text:
The people side — workspace, hiring pipeline, and new-hire onboarding.
HR & Workforce: Reviews, goals, training & certifications, time off, documents, and feedback live across these tabs — your workspace, plus team and company views for managers and HR. Recruiting and Onboarding open from the buttons up top.
Recruiting pipeline: Open a job requisition, add candidates, and move them Applied → Screening → Interview → Offer → Hired. Moving a candidate to Hired opens their onboarding record automatically — no re-keying.
Onboarding checklist: Each new hire's record holds personal info, IDs, a documents checklist (I-9, W-4, direct deposit), and background checks — with a completion gate before day one.

entries.title: Admin & setup: company, roles, import, email
entries.text:
Configure the company, control access, and get data in.
Setup Wizard: The plug-and-play wizard walks first-time configuration — company details, fiscal setup, and getting the essentials in place.
Company Settings: Company-wide preferences — identity and letterhead, fiscal year, accounting basis, and the toggles that shape how modules behave.
Roles & Permissions: Role-based access control — decide who can see and do what, module by module, and handle access requests. Permissions gate sensitive actions like MRB disposition, approvals, and payroll.
Data Import: Bring your item master and other data in from CSV/Excel with the guided wizard — migrate quickly instead of hand-keying.
Email Center: Inbound and outbound email — RFQ acknowledgements, supplier correspondence, and parsing — connected to the modules that use it.

entries.title: Your plan & billing
entries.text:
See your trial, choose a plan, and manage billing.
Plan & billing: Your trial countdown, current plan, and the tiers live here — Shop, Starter, Growth, Business, or Enterprise — with the first-year price and the standard price after 12 months on each card. The free trial is 60 days and does not require a card. After you subscribe, the first 12 months bill at the first-year price, then standard prices. Seat limits are shown on each plan.

entries.title: Plans, free Shop, trial and founding member pricing
entries.text: Shop is free for up to 5 users, with no card and no expiry. Paid Shop is for 6–10 users. Paid plans have a 60-day trial. Shop: 10 users maximum; first year $10/month first user plus $2/month each additional user; standard after year one $30/user/month. Starter: 30 users maximum; first year $250/year; standard after year one $3600/year. Growth: 100 users maximum; first year $500/year; standard after year one $8400/year. Business: 250 users maximum; first year $1000/year; standard after year one $18000/year. Enterprise: custom quote, 251+ users. A real paid subscription or trial started through March 9, 2027, 11:59 PM PT qualifies for the founding-member lifetime introductory rate. Free Shop and demos alone do not qualify. The grant is sticky across renewal and cancellation for the same workspace; it is not transferable by email. It locks the recurring rate, not seat quantity, tax or add-ons. Do not promise the lock to every signup or quote an account's actual renewal without checking Billing. Checkout/Stripe and plan eligibility remain the source of truth.
